    Fit a distance-based PERMANOVA for any supported design

    permanova.Rd

    A single front door that compiles a formula into a canonical Design Object (or accepts one directly), routes it to the engine matching its random-effect provenance and balance, and returns a result that prints as a PERMANOVA table. No denominator or permutation scheme is ever chosen silently: a design outside every supported envelope stops with a message naming the reason.

    permanova(
  formula,
  data = NULL,
  distance = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  permutations = 999L,
  mc_permutations = 9999L,
  seed = NULL,
  keep_permutations = FALSE,
  truncate = FALSE,
  max_exact = 100000L,
  tol = 1e-10
)

    Arguments

    formula

    A model formula, or a compiled `permanova_design` object. The dissimilarity may be given on the left-hand side, as in `bray ~ treatment + (1 | site)` (the idiom used by `vegan::adonis2()`), or the formula may be one-sided (`~ treatment + (1 | site)`) with the dissimilarity passed through `distance`.

    data

    A data frame with one row per observation. Ignored when `formula` is already a Design Object.

    distance

    A `dist` object or distance matrix. Needed only when the dissimilarity is not given on the formula's left-hand side.

    type

    Sum-of-squares partition for the fixed-effect terms: `"I"` (sequential), `"II"` (conditional), or `"III"` (partial). Applies to fixed-effect designs; for designs whose denominator is fixed by the random structure it is reported as not applicable.

    permutations

    A non-negative integer or `"all"`.

    mc_permutations

    Number of Monte-Carlo draws for the asymptotic `P(MC)` p-value, reported alongside `P(perm)` for designs tested in the full observation space. `P(MC)` stays smooth when the true permutation space is small (the usual case for the upper strata of a mixed design). Set to `0` to disable. Reproducible from `seed`.

    seed

    Optional random seed. Also seeds the `P(MC)` draws.

    keep_permutations

    Retain permutation statistics on the fitted object.

    truncate

    Also report zero-truncated variance components where the engine estimates them.

    max_exact

    Maximum permutation space allowed for exact enumeration.

    tol

    Numerical tolerance.

    Value

    An object of class `permanova` wrapping the engine result. Use `summary()` for the full table with variance components.

    Examples

    data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan")
bray <- vegan::vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
permanova(bray ~ Management, dune.env, permutations = 99, seed = 1)
#> Distance-based PERMANOVA
#> Engine: fixed effects  (Type I SS)
#> 
#> Factors
#>  Name       Type  Levels
#>  Management Fixed 4     
#> 
#> PERMANOVA table of results
#>  Source     df SS    MS    Pseudo-F P(perm) P(MC)  Unique perms
#>  Management 3  1.469 0.490 2.7672   0.0100  0.0051 99          
#>  Residual   16 2.830 0.177                                     
#>  Total      19 4.299
